correctness.rationale: The regular block multiplicities are 1,1,2,2. In every mixed case the 2x2 blocks are nonzero even when singular: either a reflection monomial is nonzero at each root or the two rotation evaluations cannot both vanish at reciprocal roots. For 3+1, simultaneous nontrivial determinant zeros give q1=q2, and a zero at frequency zero would then give 5ac=0. In the parallel case, any two of the three distinct-slope equations imply X=Y-Z=0; in the skew case, two nontrivial zeros imply Z=-Y and X=Y, hence L0=5Y≠0. These implications and the possible number of scalar zeros exclude all unlisted mixed ranks. In the pure case the normal form is a cubic, so there are at most three distinct fifth-root zeros. Common dilation and independent shifts of the two coset origins, plus coset exchange, are induced by rank-preserving operations. An independently written script built the regular matrices from the group law and computed exact number-field ranks and nonzero taps for all 19 normal-form witnesses. It independently enumerated the four support classes and checked orbit exhaustiveness, obtaining 10,100,50,50 and precisely the listed rank sets.
residual_risks: The supplied SVD output was inspected as recorded evidence, not used to establish exact ranks or exclusions. The claim is specific to the order-ten group and four nonzero complex coefficients.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the rank reachable with a prescribed sparse support, not a random coefficient census. The two balanced support shapes have identical tap count and coset split but different attainable ranks and different minimum ranks, so the classification gives exact attainable information loss that a support-size bound or fixed-unit spectrum cannot supply.
